title: Domain-adapted Learning and Interpretability: DRL for Gas Trading

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper applies Deep Reinforcement Learning (APEX DQN and standard DQN) to front-month NBP UK Natural Gas futures. The state space comprises candlestick price features, technical indicators (MACD, RSI, PCA, volatility-adjusted returns), and fundamental gas supply/demand features using a 3-day look-back window. The agent outputs discrete actions (buy, sell, hold) within a simulated environment featuring transaction costs, and an ensemble method (Filtered-Thresholding) is used to combine parallel agent decisions.
extraction.universe: Front-month NBP UK Natural Gas Futures contract traded on CME / virtual trading point

key_findings: Deep RL trading models outperform standard rule-based strategies and several traditional machine learning baselines (Linear Regression and Random Forest) on natural gas futures.
A sliding-window training scheme yields better performance (Sharpe Ratio of 1.32) than an anchored training window (Sharpe Ratio of 1.27) due to adapting more quickly to changing market regimes.
Adding fundamental supply/demand features does not consistently improve performance and increases performance variance due to higher noise in the observation space.
An ensemble learning scheme (Filtered-Thresholding) stabilizes agent actions, mitigates sub-optimal agent initialization risks, and enhances overall performance.
limitations: Potential performance drop when transitioning from back-testing to live trading.
Extended underwater periods could trigger an algorithmic stop before profitability is reached.
Trading frequency and holding periods must align with the operational strategy of the trading desk.
